== Research Notes ==
=== Recovered provider fields, 30 October 2026 ===
Eccles/Birgham family monument names Robert Glasgow, joiner and feuar at Leitholm, death 8 October 1800 or 1809 aged 55; wife Agnes Whitehead died 21 May 1840 aged 84. One son Thomas died April 1790 aged 8, another 27 April 1791 aged 3; Euphans died 7 April 1791 aged 5. These are two explicitly recorded sons with different deaths/ages, unlike merely repeated baptism names. Reuse the held Robert/Agnes family comparison already supported by Euphans companion 00352695. Neither son is separately created: the bounded Thomas review has not established decisive exclusions. Birth years are age-derived; ambiguous Robert year retained. Inspected provider derivative; original record/image uninspected. Companion entries are not independent witnesses. No new person, family attachment or relationship assessment change.

=== Eccles memorial identity comparison — 4 November 2026 ===
The Eccles and Birgham churchyard memorial transcript names Robert Glasgow, joiner and feuar at Leitholm, his wife [[Whitehead-9630|Agnes Whitehead]], daughter Euphans and two sons named Thomas. It gives one Thomas's death as April 1790, aged 8, and the other's as 27 April 1791, aged 3. Euphans died on 7 April 1791, aged 5. Robert's death is transcribed as 8 October 1800 or 1809, aged 55; Agnes's as 21 May 1840, aged 84. The two Thomas entries and Euphans's companion entry repeat one monument and are not independent witnesses.<ref name="EcclesMemorialTranscripts">Findmypast, ''Scotland Monumental Inscriptions'', Eccles and Birgham Churchyards, Berwickshire; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=PRS%2FSCOTLAND%2FMI%2FADD%2F5%2F00542644 Thomas Glasgow, April 1790, aged 8, PRS/SCOTLAND/MI/ADD/5/00542644] and [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=PRS%2FSCOTLAND%2FMI%2FADD%2F5%2F00542645 Thomas Glasgow, 27 April 1791, aged 3, PRS/SCOTLAND/MI/ADD/5/00542645], derivative transcripts inspected 30 October 2026; [https://findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=PRS%2FSCOTLAND%2FMI%2FADD%2F5%2F00352695 Euphans Glasgow, 7 April 1791, aged 5, PRS/SCOTLAND/MI/ADD/5/00352695], derivative transcript inspected 23 October 2026. These are companion entries from one inscription; the original monument or photograph has not been inspected.</ref>

[[Glasgow-3604|Thomas Glasgow]], recorded in an unverified profile account as born at Eccles in March 1781, remains a candidate for the elder son. March 1781 would imply about 9 years of age in April 1790, compared with the reported age of 8. This weak, unverified birth estimate does not exclude him, but the discrepancy prevents an established identification. The underlying source behind his FamilySearch tree citation needs checking. The younger son has not been assigned to an existing profile.

The ages imply that the two same-named sons' lifetimes overlapped. That unusual feature, the elder son's age discrepancy and Robert's ambiguous death year require checking against the original inscription or a photograph and the Eccles parish entries. The indexed birth years 1782 and 1788 are derived from ages at death, not recorded birth dates. The memorial's churchyard locality does not establish either son's birthplace or exact burial date. No vital date or family attachment is changed on this comparison.

=== Leitholm working-family review — 17 October 2026 ===

The inspected FamilySearch marriage index names Robert Glasgow and Agnes Whitehead at Eccles on 4 April 1779. A separately inspected baptism index names them as parents of James Glasgow, christened at Eccles on 30 December 1779. Its birth field contains only “12”, which is not a complete birthday. The source supports an earlier James child; John, born in 1786 in the captured family account, is not the first known son. The index pages are derivative records; no original register image was inspected.

Select James Glasgow (Glasgow-1238), the father recorded with Elizabath/Elizabeth Tait at Stichill, as Robert Glasgow’s possible working father, at 34%. The couple’s maintained marriage citation is dated 25 January 1740; their David and James children are indexed in June 1744 and July 1746. Robert’s estimated 1745 birth fits that family generation and could fall between those events; it is not a dated baptism. Stichill and Eccles/Leitholm belong to the same small Borders district, and the later Swinton entry attributed to the James/Tait couple offers a further local comparison. Robert’s earlier son James supplies a modest naming clue consistent with this father; a common forename cannot establish paternity. The combination favours this existing, record-defined family over the catalogue’s distant Kirknewton candidates, whose apparent proximity came from mapping Leitholm to South Leith. No inspected record names Robert as James’s son.

This is a preferred, revisable hypothesis, with 34% subjective confidence, not a measured probability or a confident connection. Robert’s 1745 birth and 8 August 1800 death each have zero attached sources on the inspected FamilySearch tree. Neither date establishes an age or place of birth. The local 1745 estimate is retained unchanged. FamilySearch attaches John Glasgow (1720–1785, GFNP-FS8) and Agnes Spark (1722–deceased, K8CD-HCW) as parents; retain that alternative without treating a contributed tree as documentary proof. The evidential basis of that parent attachment has not yet been reviewed. Do not equate that John with the much older John Glasgow-1057, husband of Agnes Spark-330, from the matching names alone. James’s brother John Glasgow-1444, christened at Stichill in 1708, is another compatible local father-generation alternative with no presently inspected Robert link. An unrecorded local father or another kinship degree remains possible. The Swinton/1740 couple continuity and Robert’s own early life need testing. Elizabeth Tait is not selected as Robert’s mother: her marriage and maternity of other children do not identify his mother. Robert is not merged with an earlier child, and James’s existing older ancestry retains its own uncertainty.

Inspect Robert’s 1779 marriage and children’s original Eccles entries for residence, occupation and witnesses, then check Leitholm feu/tenancy and joiner apprenticeship records for a named father or master. Test the contributed John/Agnes Spark account against actual records before identifying it with any local person. Recheck the 1765 Swinton household independently. James Glasgow-1222 (1777 Kelso, attributed to David Glasgow and Janet Hood) is a nearby child-name comparison for the 1779 James, not a selected identity; retain both record accounts unless a record resolves the different parents.
